shirt noun

Mir, morning routine

subūcula, subūculae f.

noun, first declension

an under-tunic or shirt

Used by Mir for an ordinary shirt.

Other words

  • tunica, tunicae f. — tunic

    noun, first declension · also used · classical

    Useful for a simple shirt by extension.

  • camisia, camisiae f. — a linen shirt or nightshirt

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Hier. Ep. 64.11; Isid. Orig. 19.22.29 (Lewis & Short); Andresian p. 38

    A Gallic word of late Latin, the source of Italian camicia and French chemise; Isidore explains it as what we sleep in.

  • indūsium, indūsiī n. — a woman’s undergarment

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Varr. LL 5.131 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 117

    Classically worn by women under other clothes; Traupman uses it for shirt.

  • subūcula cum curtīs manicīs — polo shirt

    also used · modern · Traupman 362

Examples

  • Subūculam indue.

    Put your shirt on.composed

See also undershirt, sleeve, T-shirt.
